title: Keep the pharmacy's reminders and holds right through a clock change

blocks.text: A pharmacy chain puts each filled prescription aside for the customer and sends a reminder every evening until it is picked up. Customers choose the time of their reminder, say 19:15, and the complaints start every March: the reminders arrive at 20:15. The other rule comes from the regulator: a prescription is kept for 24 hours and then goes back on the shelf, and inspectors time it.
`PickupReminders` already builds the reminder list and answers whether a hold has run out. Finish the two `TODO`s in `src/main/java/practice/PickupReminders.java`:

items: `releasedAt(heldAt)`: when a prescription put aside at `heldAt` goes back on the shelf.

blocks.text: Both keep the zone they were given. The pharmacies are in several countries, so the tests use zones whose clocks change on different dates. About two lines in total.

cases.says: in a week without a clock change, reminders come at the chosen time each day and a hold ends 24 hours after it began
across the day the clocks go forward, the next reminder is still at the chosen wall-clock time
across the day the clocks go back, a hold still ends 24 elapsed hours after it began, an hour earlier on the clock

origin.section: Duration.ofDays(1) Is 24 Hours; Period.ofDays(1) Is the Next Calendar Day

concepts: Duration.ofDays(1) is 24 elapsed hours while Period.ofDays(1) is the same wall-clock time on the next date, so across a DST change on a ZonedDateTime they differ by an hour.
